upcomingChanges.label: From 2027, the Saver's Match replaces this credit
upcomingChanges.detail: For contributions made for 2027, the Treasury pays a match of 50% of up to $2,000 into your IRA or workplace plan, rather than taking a credit off your tax, so it reaches people who owe no tax. It phases out between $41,000 and $71,000 of modified AGI on a joint return, $30,750 and $53,250 for a head of household, and $20,500 and $35,500 otherwise, and is claimed on a new Form 8880-A.

citation.sourceNote: 26 U.S.C. §6433(a)(1): a match equal to "the applicable percentage" of contributions up to $2,000. §6433(b): 50 percent, phased out over a $30,000 range above $41,000 for joint returns and surviving spouses, three-quarters of both for a head of household and half for everyone else, rounded down to whole points. Pub. L. 117-328 div. T §103(f): for "taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026". Notice 2026-48's 2027 table: the match ends at $71,000 joint and surviving spouse, $53,250 head of household, $35,500 single and married filing separately; amounts are adjusted for inflation after 2027 (§6433(h)), and it is claimed on "a new (not yet published) Form 8880-A". The notice announces proposed regulations; until they are final the engine still computes the §25B credit, which applies through 2026. Read on Cornell LII and irs.gov 2026-10-19.

citation.sourceDocument: IRS Retirement Savings Contributions Credit (Form 8880), 2026 AGI limits per IRS Notice 2025-67
citation.sourceNote: The Retirement Savings Contributions Credit (IRC §25B) is a nonrefundable credit of 50%, 20% or 10% of up to $2,000 of retirement contributions per person, and it is a CLIFF, not a phase-out: one dollar of AGI over a tier's cap drops the rate to the next step, and one dollar over the last cap ends the credit entirely. IRS Notice 2025-67 gives the 2026 caps for married filing jointly — $48,500 for the 50% rate, $52,500 for 20%, $80,500 for 10%. Single and married-filing-separately caps are half of those ($24,250 / $26,250 / $40,250) and head of household is three-quarters ($36,375 / $39,375 / $60,375), the statutory ratios §25B(b) fixes, which is also the internal check on the transcription. Omitted: the reduction for recent distributions from any retirement plan (which can wipe out the credit for someone who took money out in the testing window), the full-time-student and dependent disqualifications, the age-18 minimum, and the fact that being nonrefundable caps it at the filer's tax liability — so many households in the 50% band get less than the arithmetic suggests. Verified against IRS Notice 2025-67 on 2026-08-29.
